# Tasks Document

Tasks land in three tracks in the order the spec mandates: **A → B → C**. Within a track, tasks run sequentially (each builds on the previous). Across tracks the composite-pin tests are the actual safety net (R4.10) — sequencing is enforced by tests, not process.

Path note: the requirements/design refer to `src/multi-server.ts`; the file is actually `src/dashboard/multi-server.ts`. The runner classes live in `src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts` and `src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts`.

## Track A — Typecheck pre-computation (R2)

- [ ] 1. Create shared path denylist in src/core/path-denylist.ts
  - File: src/core/path-denylist.ts (new), src/core/__tests__/path-denylist.test.ts (new)
  - Export `partitionPaths(paths: string[]): { kept: string[]; skipped: string[] }` and `TEST_FIXTURE_SEGMENTS: readonly string[]`.
  - Implement exact-basename, basename-suffix, basename-prefix, and path-segment match per R1.5; split path segments on **both `/` and `\\`** regardless of platform.
  - Apply the case-folding rules in design.md §`path-denylist.ts`: secret-bearing entries always case-folded; lock/binary entries case-folded only on case-insensitive volumes; path-segment matches unconditionally case-insensitive.
  - Apply the narrowed test-fixture exception (R1.6): `__tests__`, `__fixtures__`, `fixtures`, `test-data`, `testdata` carve out **only** the path-segment denylist; basename/suffix/prefix rules still apply.
  - Tests cover per-category folding rules, narrowed fixture exception, and **mixed-separator inputs** (Linux runtime + `secrets\\foo.json`; Windows runtime + `secrets/foo.json` — both must be skipped).
  - Purpose: shared filter consumed by diff (Track B), typecheck output filtering (Track A), and hygiene-signals (Track B); single source of match semantics so behavior is identical at every callsite.
  - _Leverage: node:path only — no new runtime deps._
  - _Requirements: R1.5, R1.6, NFR Code Architecture (denylist co-located)_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in cross-platform path handling and security-adjacent matchers | Task: Create the shared `partitionPaths` matcher in src/core/path-denylist.ts implementing R1.5 (exact basename, suffix, prefix, path-segment) and R1.6 (narrowed fixture exception), with the case-folding matrix from design.md §`path-denylist.ts`, plus its co-located vitest suite. Mark task 1 [-] in tasks.md before starting; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard task review via the dashboard Tasks page; only after the review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: NOT shell globs, NOT git pathspec wildcards — exact + suffix/prefix + segment only; no new runtime deps; do not import from src/tools/ — this is a leaf utility | _Leverage: node:path | _Requirements: R1.5, R1.6 | Success: partitionPaths returns identical results for the same inputs across separator choices; case-folding rules match the design matrix; fixture exception applies only to path-segment matches; tests exercise mixed-separator inputs and the narrowed exception._

- [ ] 2. Create adversarial-settings helper in src/core/adversarial-settings.ts
  - File: src/core/adversarial-settings.ts (new), src/core/__tests__/adversarial-settings.test.ts (new)
  - Export `loadSettings(projectPath)`, `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner: 'adversarial' | 'taskReview')`, and `isTypecheckEnabled(settings)`.
  - `loadSettings`: in-process cache keyed by `(absPath, mtime, size)`; **read-throw containment** wrapping `statSync`/`readFileSync` for at minimum `EBUSY`/`EACCES`/`EISDIR`/`ELOOP`/`ENOENT`/other (R3.7). `ENOENT` returns `{}` silently; all other I/O errors and parse failures return `{}` AND emit a warn-once with the **pinned format** in R3.7. Warn-once flag per absPath, cleared when `(mtime, size)` advances.
  - `resolveRunnerModel`: grouped non-empty string > legacy non-empty string > `undefined` (R3.1–R3.4). Empty string is "explicitly cleared" → fall through (R3.5). `null` runner block treated as absent. Non-object runner block ignored with warn-once. Non-string `model` ignored with warn-once (R3.5). Unknown sub-keys silently ignored (forward-compat).
  - `isTypecheckEnabled`: `false` only when `features.typecheck === false`; non-boolean values warn-once and default to `true` (R3.12).
  - Tests pin the R3.10 precedence matrix (a–g), automated `utimes()` mid-session edit, **read-throw containment** (`EBUSY`/`EACCES`/`EISDIR`/`ELOOP` simulated via `vi.spyOn(fs, 'readFileSync')`), `isTypecheckEnabled` non-boolean warn, `resolveRunnerModel` non-string `model` warn, and a cold-cache integration test (timed first call, regression bound).
  - Purpose: single source of truth for settings reads, model resolution, and feature flags; consumed by Track A (`isTypecheckEnabled`) and Track C (`resolveRunnerModel`) — landing it now means Track C is wiring-only.
  - _Leverage: node:fs (statSync/readFileSync), node:path._
  - _Requirements: R3.1–R3.10, R3.12, NFR Reliability (read-throw containment), NFR Performance (settings read < 5 ms warm)_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in JSON schema tolerance, mtime+size cache keys, and process-lifetime warn-once semantics | Task: Implement loadSettings (cache + read-throw containment), resolveRunnerModel (grouped > legacy > undefined precedence), and isTypecheckEnabled in src/core/adversarial-settings.ts plus its vitest suite covering R3.10's full precedence matrix, mid-session utimes() edit, read-throw simulation, and the warn-once-per-(absPath) flag eviction on mtime/size advance. Mark task 2 [-] in tasks.md before starting; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard task review; only after review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: No I/O throw escapes loadSettings; warning format must match R3.7 byte-for-byte (it is a contract); cache must use both mtime AND size to handle second-resolution mtime filesystems (NFS/SMB/WSL2 mounts); do NOT eagerly migrate legacy `model` field — both shapes are accepted indefinitely | _Leverage: node:fs, node:path | _Requirements: R3.1–R3.10, R3.12 | Success: precedence matrix tests pass; warn-once persists per absPath until (mtime, size) advances; ENOENT silent / other I/O warns; isTypecheckEnabled defaults to true; cold-cache call < 15 ms typical._

- [ ] 3. Create typecheck utility in src/core/typecheck.ts
  - File: src/core/typecheck.ts (new), src/core/__tests__/typecheck.test.ts (new)
  - Export `runProjectTypecheck(projectPath, allFiles, opts: { enabled }): Promise<TypecheckResult[]>` returning the discriminated union from R2.2 + design §`typecheck.ts` (`success` | `unavailable` | `timeout`, with `unavailable.reason` enumerating `'no-tsconfig' | 'project-references' | 'wrapper-config' | 'tsc-not-found' | 'no-parseable-output' | 'output-overflow' | 'feature-disabled' | 'rejection'`).
  - Tsconfig gate: root `tsconfig.json` only; `"references"` or `"files": []` with no `"include"` → `'wrapper-config'` / `'project-references'`. `tsc` resolved from `node_modules/.bin/tsc`; absent → `'tsc-not-found'`.
  - Pre-spawn `await fs.promises.mkdir(<projectPath>/.spec-workflow/.cache, { recursive: true })`. Spawn `tsc --noEmit -p <projectPath> --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile <projectPath>/.spec-workflow/.cache/tsc.tsbuildinfo --listFiles --pretty false` with `env: { ...process.env, FORCE_COLOR: '0', NO_COLOR: '1' }`, `maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024`, 30s timeout (SIGTERM → 2s grace → SIGKILL).
  - **Two-pass parser** (design §`typecheck.ts`): Pass 1 walks lines, opens a diagnostic on `^(.+?)\((\d+),(\d+)\): error TS(\d+): (.+)$`, then appends whitespace-led non-path lines to that diagnostic's `message` (joined with `\n`); stops on next diagnostic, abs-path-shaped line, or EOF. Pass 2 keeps absolute-path-shaped lines (Win `^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]`, POSIX `^/`) from lines not consumed by Pass 1.
  - Async path normalization (R2.4): chunked `fs.promises.realpath` (100 paths/chunk), per-path `try/catch` for ENOENT (bucket as excluded using original path); case-fold to lowercase on case-insensitive volumes (`process.platform === 'darwin' || 'win32'`). Reported `coverage.compiled` / `coverage.excluded` use **original `allFiles` paths** (deduped by normalized form, first-seen original).
  - Tag each diagnostic with `inScope = (normalized file ∈ normalized allFiles)`. Apply `partitionPaths` to `coverage.compiled`, `coverage.excluded`, `diagnostics[].file`; surface dropped count as `suppressedDenylistedFiles`. Cap diagnostics at 100 (in-scope first).
  - Failure mapping per R2.8/R2.9/R2.11 + design Error Scenarios §1–6: timeout → `'timeout'`, `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER` → `'output-overflow'`, non-zero exit + zero parsed diagnostics → `'no-parseable-output'`, clean exit + empty `--listFiles` → `'no-parseable-output'` (NOT silent "everything excluded").
  - Tests cover: clean success, in-scope/out-of-scope tagging, partial coverage, every `'unavailable'` reason, `'timeout'`, `'output-overflow'`, pnpm symlinked path normalization fixture, 100-diagnostic cap, output-side denylist filtering, **multi-line diagnostic continuation** (TS2345 type-expansion across 4+ lines — assert joined `message` contains both head and expansion), abs-path-in-error-message excluded from compiled set, per-path ENOENT degrades to excluded, **first-run cache-dir creation**.
  - _Leverage: src/core/path-denylist.ts (Task 1), node:child_process (execFile), node:fs/promises, node:path._
  - _Requirements: R2.1–R2.14, NFR Performance (incremental < 5s, cold < 30s timeout), NFR Reliability (utility never throws)_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in child-process orchestration, tsc compiler diagnostics, and cross-platform path normalization | Task: Implement runProjectTypecheck in src/core/typecheck.ts with the two-pass parser, chunked async realpath normalization, denylist-filtered output, full failure-mode mapping, and 30s timeout (SIGTERM → 2s grace → SIGKILL); plus its vitest suite covering every reason code, multi-line diagnostic continuation, pnpm symlink fixtures, and first-run cache-dir creation. Mark task 3 [-] in tasks.md; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard review; only after review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: tsc invoked via node_modules/.bin/tsc — NEVER imported as a library; utility must NEVER throw out of handlePrepare (catch every shape and convert to a result); coverage arrays use original paths, deduped by normalized form (first-seen wins); per-path realpath try/catch for ENOENT — do NOT bulk-realpath and let one missing file fail the chunk | _Leverage: src/core/path-denylist.ts | _Requirements: R2.1–R2.14 | Success: every R2 reason code reachable via tests; coverage paths match what the agent recorded (not the realpath'd form); 30s timeout terminates cleanly; multi-line diagnostic continuation joins with \n; --listFiles parse-failure surfaces as 'no-parseable-output' rather than degrading to "everything excluded"._

- [ ] 4. Wire Promise.allSettled orchestration + validateAllFiles + unwrap helpers + typecheck data fields into handlePrepare
  - File: src/tools/review-task.ts (modify), src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts (extend)
  - After `allFiles` is computed, add the `validateAllFiles` helper from design §`validateAllFiles`: per-element try/catch around `path.resolve` + symlink-resolved inside-projectPath check (`safeRealpath(resolved)` vs `safeRealpath(projectPath)`); drop NUL-byte paths, non-string entries, paths outside projectPath, and symlinks pointing outside, each with warn-once. Preserve symlink-original path in the kept list (reviewer sees what the agent recorded). `safeRealpath` swallows ENOENT and returns `undefined`.
  - Add the `Promise.allSettled` shell wrapping `computeTaskDiff` (placeholder this task — pass-through that returns the empty-diff state until Task 8 implements it), `runProjectTypecheck`, and `computeHygieneSignals`. **Track A lands the shell with `runProjectTypecheck` populated; the diff slot is wired but inert until Track B.**
  - Add `unwrapDiff` / `unwrapTypecheck` / `unwrapHygiene` helpers per design §`unwrap*`. Rejection states: diff → `{ diff: '', stats: undefined, skippedPaths: [], truncated: false, rejection: { message } }`; typecheck → `[{ tsconfigPath, status: 'unavailable', reason: 'rejection', rejectionMessage }]`; hygiene → `{ signals: [], rejection: { message } }`. Warn-once key `(utility, error.message)` so heterogeneous causes get distinct logs.
  - Extend `data` shape with `typecheckResults` and `hygieneRejection` (and `diff`/`diffStats`/`skippedPaths`/`diffTruncated`/`diffRejection` slots, populated as empty in the interim — Track B fills these). `filesToReview = validatedAllFiles`.
  - Read settings via `loadSettings(projectPath)` (Task 2); pass `{ enabled: isTypecheckEnabled(settings) }` to `runProjectTypecheck`.
  - Tests: validateAllFiles boundary cases (NUL-byte, non-string, relative path, outside-projectPath, symlink-outside, deleted-file ENOENT, duplicates, non-array input — each surface in cleaned list and warn-once log); concurrency assertion using start/finish-time spies; **all-three-utilities rejection tests** (stub each in turn, assert `data.diffRejection.message` / `typecheckResults[0].reason === 'rejection'` / `data.hygieneRejection.message`); unwrap warn-once heterogeneity test (two distinct errors from same utility, both logged).
  - _Leverage: src/core/typecheck.ts (Task 3), src/core/adversarial-settings.ts (Task 2), src/core/hygiene-signals.ts (existing — denylist filter added in Task 7)._
  - _Requirements: R2.12, NFR Reliability (utility never throws, internal try/catch in both prelude steps), Error Scenarios §13, §14_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in async orchestration and exception-tolerant input validation | Task: Add validateAllFiles, the Promise.allSettled shell, unwrap* helpers, and the new data fields to handlePrepare in src/tools/review-task.ts; populate typecheckResults from runProjectTypecheck; leave the diff slot wired-but-inert (Track B fills it). Extend the integration test to cover validateAllFiles boundary cases, concurrency timing, all-three rejection routing, and the heterogeneous warn-once key. Mark task 4 [-] in tasks.md; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard review; only after review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: handlePrepare must NEVER spawn a child process directly — all process work lives in utility modules; both validateAllFiles and loadSettings have internal try/catch — no synchronous throw escapes the prelude; symlink-resolve BOTH the entry and projectPath before the prefix check (Finding 12); preserve the symlink-original path in the kept list (reviewer-visible) | _Leverage: Task 3 (typecheck), Task 2 (settings), existing computeHygieneSignals | _Requirements: R2.12, Error Scenarios §13, §14 | Success: handlePrepare resolves under every utility-rejection scenario; data.typecheckResults populated; diff slot returns the empty-diff shape; warn-once key (utility, error.message) emits two logs for two distinct errors._

- [ ] 5. Emit Track-A typecheck directives in buildReviewMethodology + interim composite-pin fixtures
  - File: src/tools/review-task.ts (modify `buildReviewMethodology`), src/tools/__tests__/__fixtures__/methodology/*.txt (new — 7 typecheck-axis fixtures), src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts (extend with composite-pin tests + drift test)
  - Extend `buildReviewMethodology` signature with `typecheckState: TypecheckMethodologyState` (`success-clean-full | success-with-diagnostics | success-partial-coverage | success-with-diagnostics-and-partial-coverage | unavailable-feature-disabled | unavailable-other (with reason) | timeout`). Diff state stays absent in Track A — interim composite is "Track A directives only."
  - Emit R4.4 (typecheck-present), R4.5 (typecheck-partial-coverage — composes with R4.4 when diagnostics + partial both present), R4.6a (feature-disabled), R4.6b (other-unavailable, with reason in prose), R4.7 (timeout) **verbatim** from requirements.md §R4. Authority direction is reversed (R4 prose is authoritative, fixtures derived).
  - Number directives per design §`buildReviewMethodology`: items 1–8 unchanged, item 9 hygiene unchanged, **item 10 typecheck**.
  - Ship 7 typecheck-axis composite-pin fixtures in `src/tools/__tests__/__fixtures__/methodology/` (this is the first `__fixtures__` dir): `success-clean-full.txt`, `success-with-diagnostics.txt`, `success-partial-coverage.txt`, `success-with-diagnostics-and-partial-coverage.txt`, `unavailable-feature-disabled.txt`, `unavailable-other.txt`, `timeout.txt`. Each fixture's docstring records the redundancy/composition concern it pins. **Tag every Track-A interim fixture with the marker `# SPEC-WORKFLOW:TRACK-A:INTERIM-PIN`** — Track B's PR (Task 9) replaces these.
  - Composite-pin normalization: line-by-line `.trimEnd()`, unified `\n`, NFC, em-dash → hyphen, smart quotes → straight, **whitespace-run collapse to single space** (applied to both sides). Pin the full `buildReviewMethodology(...)` return value, not directive substrings.
  - Add the **two-way drift test** (R4.10 §"Two-way drift test") with `EXPECTED_R4_BLOCK_COUNT = 5` for the Track-A interim (R4.4, R4.5, R4.6a, R4.6b, R4.7). Extractor matches both `> ...` block-quote and ``` ```...``` ``` fenced-block delimiters; partial-extraction must fail, not silently reduce coverage.
  - _Leverage: requirements.md §R4 (verbatim source), Task 4 data fields._
  - _Requirements: R4.4, R4.5, R4.6a, R4.6b, R4.7, R4.8, R4.9, R4.10_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in deterministic-prose composition and unicode-stable test fixtures | Task: Extend buildReviewMethodology to emit R4.4–R4.7 verbatim per the typecheckState discriminated union, ship the 7 typecheck-axis composite-pin fixtures (each tagged with the SPEC-WORKFLOW:TRACK-A:INTERIM-PIN marker), and add the two-way drift test with EXPECTED_R4_BLOCK_COUNT = 5 for the Track-A interim. Mark task 5 [-] in tasks.md; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard review; only after review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: R4 prose in requirements.md is AUTHORITATIVE — if a fixture and R4 disagree, fix the fixture; normalization MUST apply to both sides of every comparison; partial extraction (delimiter format change) MUST fail the test, not silently reduce coverage; do NOT pin directive substrings — pin the full composite output | _Leverage: requirements.md §R4 verbatim, Task 4 typecheckState wiring | _Requirements: R4.4–R4.10 | Success: 7 fixtures pin every typecheck axis; both drift directions pass; EXPECTED_R4_BLOCK_COUNT guard rejects partial extraction; every interim fixture carries the SPEC-WORKFLOW:TRACK-A:INTERIM-PIN marker._

## Track B — Diff-first context (R1)

- [ ] 6. Create task-diff utility in src/core/task-diff.ts
  - File: src/core/task-diff.ts (new), src/core/__tests__/task-diff.test.ts (new)
  - Export `computeTaskDiff(projectPath, allFiles): Promise<TaskDiffResult>` per design §`task-diff.ts` (`{ diff, stats, skippedPaths, truncated, rejection? }`).
  - `partitionPaths(allFiles)` → kept + skipped. Run `git diff -U10 -M HEAD --` and `git diff --numstat HEAD --` **concurrently** with `cwd: projectPath`, `env: { ...process.env, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS: '0' }`, kept paths as pathspec, `maxBuffer: 16 * 1024 * 1024`.
  - Strip `Binary files ... differ` sections from the unified-diff body (R1.5 binary handling). Numstat is the canonical source for `diffStats`; never parse the unified-diff body for counts.
  - Two-phase truncation (R1.9): per-file cap 500 added+removed lines from numstat → replace hunks with `<diff truncated: <file> per-file cap exceeded>`; total cap 50,000 bytes after per-file truncation → replace remaining files in pathspec order with `<diff truncated: <file> total budget exhausted, file truncated despite size>`. Set `truncated: true` if either fires.
  - Expected-failure mapping: `execFile` rejection / non-zero exit / `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER` / not-a-git-repo / `git` missing → return `{ diff: '', stats: undefined, skippedPaths, truncated: false }` with NO `rejection` field. The `rejection` field is **only** set by the orchestrator's `unwrapDiff` when an unexpected throw escapes (R4.2b vs R4.2a split).
  - Tests: empty repo, basic hunks, denylist filtering, binary-stripping, per-file-cap message, total-budget message (synthesize via small budget knob exposed for tests if needed), `git` missing, non-zero exit, `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER` synthesized via `maxBuffer: 1024`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` env propagation assertion.
  - _Leverage: src/core/path-denylist.ts (Task 1), node:child_process (execFile)._
  - _Requirements: R1.1, R1.2, R1.4, R1.5 (binary), R1.7–R1.11, NFR Performance (< 200 ms / 50 files), NFR Reliability_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in git plumbing, byte-budget truncation, and child-process orchestration | Task: Implement computeTaskDiff in src/core/task-diff.ts with concurrent git diff + numstat invocation, two-phase truncation, binary-section stripping, and full expected-failure-to-empty-result mapping; plus its vitest suite covering every R1 failure mode and the GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 propagation. Mark task 6 [-] in tasks.md; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard review; only after review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: NEVER parse the unified-diff body for stats — numstat is canonical; expected failures must NOT set rejection (that is reserved for the orchestrator's unwrapDiff path — R4.2a vs R4.2b are structurally distinct); -M flag enabled even though pathspec defeats some rename detection (the directive tells the reviewer not to trust diff for renames); maxBuffer 16 MB | _Leverage: Task 1 (path-denylist) | _Requirements: R1.1–R1.11 | Success: every R1 failure mode degrades to empty diff with no rejection field; truncation messages are byte-stable and match R1.9 verbatim; numstat drives diffStats; binary sections stripped from body._

- [ ] 7. Extend hygiene-signals to denylist-filter via partitionPaths
  - File: src/core/hygiene-signals.ts (modify), src/core/__tests__/hygiene-signals.test.ts (extend)
  - Filter `files` through `partitionPaths(files).kept` before scanning. Public signature unchanged (R1.5 closing-the-known-gap).
  - Tests assert that denylisted files are not scanned (e.g. a `.env` or `package-lock.json` in the input list never appears in the returned signals) and that fixture-exception paths are still scanned.
  - _Leverage: src/core/path-denylist.ts (Task 1), existing computeHygieneSignals + tests._
  - _Requirements: R1.5 (denylist shared with hygiene), NFR Code Architecture (denylist co-located + shared)_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in additive refactors and test-stable public signatures | Task: Apply partitionPaths to the input list inside computeHygieneSignals before scanning, keeping the public signature unchanged; extend the existing vitest suite with denylist-skipped and fixture-exception cases. Mark task 7 [-] in tasks.md; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard review; only after review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: Public signature is FROZEN — only the body changes; the denylist applies to BOTH diff and hygiene paths (one source of truth in path-denylist.ts) | _Leverage: Task 1 (path-denylist), existing hygiene-signals tests | _Requirements: R1.5 | Success: denylisted files are never scanned; existing tests still pass; fixture-exception paths are still scanned (so a PR modifying path-denylist itself reviews through this surface)._

- [ ] 8. Add diff to handlePrepare's Promise.allSettled + emit diff data fields
  - File: src/tools/review-task.ts (modify handlePrepare's Promise.allSettled call), src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts (extend)
  - Replace the inert diff slot from Task 4 with `computeTaskDiff(projectPath, validatedAllFiles)`. `unwrapDiff` from Task 4 already converts unexpected rejection to `data.diffRejection` (utility-throw path → R4.2b); expected failures from Task 6 return the empty-diff shape without `rejection` (benign empty path → R4.2a).
  - Populate `data.diff`, `data.diffStats`, `data.skippedPaths`, `data.diffTruncated`, `data.diffRejection` per design §`data shape additions`. `filesToReview` retains its current shape — additive (R1.10).
  - Extend integration tests: end-to-end prepare with uncommitted changes (assert `data.diff` non-empty + `diffStats` populated); diff-empty branch (no working-tree changes — assert `data.diff === ""` and no `diffRejection`); diff-rejection branch (stub `computeTaskDiff` to throw — assert `data.diffRejection.message` is set, distinguishing from the empty branch); concurrency assertion remains green.
  - _Leverage: src/core/task-diff.ts (Task 6), Task 4's unwrapDiff + Promise.allSettled shell._
  - _Requirements: R1.1–R1.11, R2.12 (concurrency)_
  - _Prompt: Implement the task for spec tighter-reviews, first run spec-workflow-guide to get the workflow guide then implement the task: Role: TypeScript Developer with expertise in additive integration changes that preserve test stability | Task: Replace the inert diff slot from Task 4 with computeTaskDiff in handlePrepare's Promise.allSettled, populate the diff data fields, and extend the integration test with the diff-empty / diff-present / diff-rejection branches. Mark task 8 [-] in tasks.md; on completion run log-implementation and request a dashboard review; only after review passes mark [x] | Restrictions: filesToReview shape is FROZEN — additive only at the data-shape level; benign empty diff (no working-tree changes, not a git repo, etc.) MUST NOT set data.diffRejection — that field distinguishes utility-throw from empty (R4.2a vs R4.2b); concurrency wall-clock = max(diff, typecheck, hygiene) — assert via start/finish-time spies | _Leverage: Task 6 (computeTaskDiff), Task 4 (unwrapDiff + Promise.allSettled) | _Requirements: R1.1–R1.11 | Success: data.diff populated for non-empty working trees; data.diffStats from numstat; data.skippedPaths reports denylist exclusions; data.diffRejection ONLY appears on utility-throw, never on benign empty; diff-empty and diff-rejection tests pass distinctly._

- [ ] 9. Replace interim methodology pins with Track-B preamble + diff axis + cross-axis fixtures + drift-test guard updates
  - File: src/tools/review-task.ts (modify `buildReviewMethodology`), src/tools/__tests__/__fixtures__/methodology/*.txt (replace ALL Track-A interim fixtures + add diff axis + cross-axis pins), src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts (extend)
  - Extend `buildReviewMethodology` signature with `diffState: DiffMethodologyState` (`present | present-truncated | empty | rejected (with message)`).
  - Emit the unnumbered preamble `**Read first:**` per design §`buildReviewMethodology` composition order: R4.1 (present), R4.2a (empty / benign), R4.2b (rejected — surfaces `data.diffRejection.message`), or R4.1 + truncation note (present-truncated).
